title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
abstract: How can we predict which base checkpoint is worth an expensive round of agentic post-training? End-to-end pass@$K$ tests whether successful behavior already appears in a base model's distribution, but it is a poor fit for agentic coding: many base checkpoints cannot reliably produce the well-formed tool invocation required to complete a task end-to-end. Single-shot or short-horizon tasks avoid these tool-calling failures by collapsing a multi-step interaction into a fixed prompt and a single patch, but they sidestep the core capability we care about: maintaining coherent state over many tool-using steps as the repository evolves. To bridge this gap, we treat successful post-trained agent trajectories as a lookahead signal of base-model potential. Replaying each trajectory and rerunning tests after every code-changing step identifies the decisive step: the first step whose cumulative patch flips the repository from failing to passing, certifying that the recorded action solves the task given the prior context. Motivated by a coverage principle for agentic traces, we build three screens at this step that do not require a base checkpoint to drive the harness from a cold start: (i) Decisive-Action BPB (bits per byte) measures the probability mass on the certified action, (ii) Patch MCQ tests the checkpoint's choice between that action and alternatives rejected by the same verifier, and (iii) prefix-conditioned pass@$K$ evaluates support for functionally-correct generations and credits any continuation that the tests accept. Across ten pairs of public base and post-trained models, all three screens rank the cohort in close agreement with post-trained SWE-bench Verified pass@$1$. As our methods need only a benchmark's successful trajectories and its verifier, they can be applied to turn future agentic coding benchmarks into base-model evaluations.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In Advanced Methods for Coding Agents, we ask how to measure capability before a model has been trained to act like an agent. Today's lecture is on “Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models.” The study comes from a team at NVIDIA, with coauthor Jiantao Jiao also affiliated with the University of California, Berkeley. The central puzzle is practical: can we predict which base checkpoints are worth post-training? I see Noah’s hand—go ahead, Noah.
segments.zh: 在《编程智能体的进阶方法》这门课里，我们要问的是：在一个模型还没被训练成智能体之前，怎么衡量它的能力。今天的讲座主题是“在它们能解题之前：从基础模型预测训练后的编程智能体表现”。这项研究来自英伟达的一个团队，共同作者焦剑涛还隶属于加州大学伯克利分校。核心问题很实际：我们能不能预测哪些基础检查点值得做后训练？我看到诺亚举手了，诺亚你说。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor, why evaluate a base model using another agent’s successful trajectory?
segments.zh: 教授您好，为什么要用另一个智能体的成功轨迹来评估基础模型呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Because the field is moving toward richer evaluations of agents, but those tests can confound coding skill with the ability to follow a particular tool protocol. Work such as PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation and EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction explores ways to make costly agent evaluation more efficient. This paper takes a different angle: it uses verified steps from successful trajectories to probe what a base model can do. That matters when full post-training runs are expensive.
segments.zh: 因为整个领域正朝着更丰富的智能体评估方向发展，但这些测试可能会把编程能力和遵循特定工具协议的能力混在一起。像PACE：智能体能力评估的代理指标和EarlyEval：通过早期结果预测实现更廉价的智能体评估这类工作，探索的是如何让昂贵的智能体评估变得更高效。这篇论文走的是另一条路：它利用成功轨迹中经过验证的步骤，来探测基座模型能做到什么。当完整的后训练成本很高时，这一点就很重要。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The authors contrast repository-level agent benchmarks with bounded coding tests. A benchmark such as SWE-bench Verified asks an agent to work through a real repository task, often using tools across multiple steps. Base models can score near zero there, even when they possess useful coding knowledge, because they may not follow the harness’s interaction format. Function-generation tests are easier to run on base models, but they do not capture sustained work in a changing repository. The paper seeks a bridge between these evaluation settings.
segments.zh: 作者把仓库级智能体基准和有边界的编程测试做了对比。像SWE-bench Verified这样的基准，要求智能体完成一个真实的仓库任务，往往要跨多步使用工具。基座模型在这类任务上可能几乎得零分，哪怕它们其实具备有用的编程知识，因为它们可能不遵循测试框架的交互格式。函数生成测试在基座模型上更容易跑，但捕捉不到在不断变化的仓库中持续工作的能力。这篇论文想在这两类评测设置之间搭一座桥。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: does the method ask the base model to solve the whole repository task?
segments.zh: 快速问一下：这个方法会让基础模型解决整个仓库任务吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. It conditions the base model on context from a successful agent’s trajectory, then evaluates its response at a point where a resolving action is available. The authors use the task’s executable verifier, usually tests, to locate the first code-changing step after which the accumulated patch passes. They call this the decisive step, and the successful action there the golden action. The evaluation measures whether a base checkpoint supports that useful action, rather than whether it can independently discover the whole path.
segments.zh: 不是。它把成功智能体轨迹中的上下文作为条件提供给基础模型，然后在某个已有可解决问题的动作可用的节点上评估其响应。作者利用任务的可执行验证器（通常是测试）来定位第一个代码变更步骤，使得在此之后累积的补丁能够通过验证。他们把这个步骤称为决定性步骤，把该步骤上的成功动作称为黄金动作。这种评估衡量的是基础检查点是否支持那个有用的动作，而不是它能否独立发现整条路径。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That distinction is central. Imagine joining a debugging session after a colleague has already inspected the code and narrowed down the defect. You still need to recognize or produce the change that fixes it, but you are not being tested on the earlier investigation. The paper uses trajectory prefixes to provide that context. This makes the probe more agentic than isolated code completion, while avoiding the cold-start interaction failure that can obscure a base model’s coding ability.
segments.zh: 这个区别很关键。想象一下，你加入一个调试会话时，同事已经看过了代码并缩小了缺陷范围。你仍然需要识别或写出修复它的改动，但不会考察你前面的排查过程。论文用轨迹前缀来提供这种上下文。这让探测比孤立的代码补全更有智能体特性，同时避免了冷启动交互失败，这种失败可能会掩盖基础模型的编码能力。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Can you clarify how the authors decide that an action really resolves the issue?
segments.zh: 你能说明一下作者是怎么判断某个动作确实解决了这个问题的吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: They replay code-changing steps against the repository and run the task verifier on the cumulative patch. The decisive step is the earliest one whose resulting repository state passes. The golden action is then applied to the preceding state, so it has a concrete, test-based success criterion. To reduce repeated verifier runs, the authors use binary search over code-changing steps. That procedure assumes later cumulative patches remain passing; when that assumption fails, a linear search is available.
segments.zh: 他们会把改代码的步骤在仓库上重放，并对累积补丁运行任务验证器。决定性的步骤是最早让仓库状态通过验证的那一步。然后把这个黄金动作应用到前一个状态上，这样它就有了一个具体的、基于测试的成功标准。为了减少重复运行验证器，作者对改代码的步骤用了二分查找。这个流程假设后面的累积补丁仍然能通过；当这个假设不成立时，也可以用线性查找。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The paper introduces 3 probes. Decisive-Action B-P-B scores the probability a base checkpoint assigns to the golden action, with a byte-normalized negative log-likelihood. Patch M-C-Q asks the model to select that action over plausible alternatives rejected by the verifier. Prefix-conditioned pass at K instead lets the base model generate continuations from the trajectory prefix and checks whether any sampled continuation succeeds. Together, these probes test recognition, discrimination, and generation.
segments.zh: 这篇论文提出了3种探针。Decisive-Action B-P-B 用字节归一化的负对数似然，给基础检查点分配给黄金动作的概率打分。Patch M-C-Q 则让模型在若干看似合理、但被验证器否决的备选动作中选出那个正确动作。而 Prefix-conditioned pass at K 是让基础模型从轨迹前缀出发生成后续内容，然后检查采样出的续写里是否有任何一个能成功。这三种探针合在一起，分别测试了识别、区分和生成能力。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Another question: why use byte normalization and rotate the multiple-choice options?
segments.zh: 还有一个问题：为什么要用字节归一化，还要轮换多选题的选项顺序？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Byte normalization makes the action-likelihood score more comparable across models whose tokenizers split the same text differently. For Patch M-C-Q, the distractors are actions generated by other models and rejected by the same task verifier in the same preceding state. The options are presented together, and their positions are cyclically rotated; answer-letter likelihoods are aggregated across those rotations to limit position bias. The authors also test whether adding generated reasoning before the answer changes the result.
segments.zh: 字节归一化让动作似然分数在那些对同一段文本切分方式不同的模型之间更具可比性。对于 Patch M-C-Q，干扰项是其他模型生成的、并且在相同前序状态下被同一个任务验证器拒绝的动作。这些选项会一起呈现，位置会循环轮换；答案字母的似然会在这些轮换之间聚合，以限制位置偏差。作者还测试了在答案前加入生成的推理是否会改变结果。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: For prefix-conditioned pass at K, the harness takes over at the decisive step and samples 8, 16, or 32 continuations. A bridge translates base-model outputs into the harness’s expected tool interface, and a continuation can include up to 3 generated steps. So these results describe a model-and-harness system under that bridge, not a model response in isolation. The setup also uses trajectories from multiple agent systems and coding benchmarks, then compares probe scores with paired post-trained models.
segments.zh: 对于前缀条件下的K次通过，测试框架会在关键步骤接管，并采样8、16或32个续写。一个桥接层会把基础模型的输出转换成测试框架所期望的工具接口，而一次续写最多可以包含3个生成步骤。所以这些结果描述的是在该桥接层下的模型加测试框架系统，而不是孤立的模型响应。这个设置还使用了来自多个智能体系统和编程基准的轨迹，然后把探针分数与配对的后训练模型进行比较。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hold on, does a larger sampling budget always make the ranking more reliable?
segments.zh: 等一下，采样预算越大，排名就一定越可靠吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. On SWE-bench Verified-derived prefixes, pass at 8 and pass at 16 both have a Spearman rank correlation of 0.988 with post-trained performance, while pass at 32 reaches 0.906. With DeepSWE trajectories, the decisive-action B-P-B correlation is 0.964, Patch M-C-Q is 0.867, and pass at 32 is 0.951. These are strong associations in a cohort of 10 model families, but they are not guarantees for a new checkpoint.
segments.zh: 不是。在SWE-bench Verified衍生的前缀上，pass@8和pass@16与后训练性能的Spearman秩相关都是0.988，而pass@32则降到0.906。在DeepSWE轨迹上，决定性动作的B-P-B相关性是0.964，Patch M-C-Q是0.867，pass@32是0.951。在一个包含10个模型家族的队列中，这些都是很强的关联，但对一个新的检查点来说，它们并不构成保证。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The probes also correlate with post-trained performance on SWE-bench Multilingual and Terminal-Bench 2.1, though the pattern varies by target. DeepSWE-derived B-P-B reaches 0.976 on the multilingual benchmark, while pass at 32 reaches 0.930 on Terminal-Bench. Meanwhile, conventional tests are inconsistent predictors: HumanEval has a negative rank correlation, and RepoBench XFirst is more informative but still weaker than several proposed probes. This suggests that trajectory context and executable verification capture something the bounded tests can miss.
segments.zh: 这些探针在SWE-bench多语言版和Terminal-Bench 2.1上也与后训练性能相关，不过具体模式因目标而异。DeepSWE衍生的B-P-B在多语言基准上达到0.976，而pass at 32在Terminal-Bench上达到0.930。与此同时，传统测试作为预测指标并不一致：HumanEval呈负的秩相关，RepoBench XFirst信息量更大，但仍弱于若干提出的探针。这表明轨迹上下文和可执行验证捕捉到了有界测试可能遗漏的东西。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How should we interpret those correlations, given the small cohort and different training recipes?
segments.zh: 考虑到样本量这么小、训练配方又各不相同，我们该怎么解读这些相关性呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Cautiously. The main comparisons use only 10 checkpoint families, with post-trained models developed under different recipes and sometimes different harnesses. The paper reports point estimates without confidence intervals. Also, a trajectory-derived probe conditions on another agent’s successful investigation; it does not show that a base model can find that state on its own. A controlled fine-tuning check on 3 checkpoints preserves the probe-predicted ordering, but that small consistency check cannot establish broad predictive accuracy.
segments.zh: 谨慎看待。主要对比只用了10个检查点系列，后训练模型是在不同配方、有时甚至是不同测试框架下开发的。论文报告的是点估计，没有置信区间。此外，从轨迹推导出的探针依赖于另一个智能体成功的调查过程；它并不能表明基础模型自己能找到那个状态。对3个检查点做的受控微调验证保持了探针预测的排序，但这个小规模的一致性检查无法确立广泛的预测准确性。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The broader contribution is a way to turn successful agent trajectories into evaluations of base checkpoints, provided a benchmark has executable verifiers. It complements work on agent evaluation by asking a different question: not only whether a completed agent succeeds, but whether a less-trained model can recognize or produce a verified solution step when given relevant context. Future studies should use larger cohorts, more controlled post-training, and trajectories matched to each target task family. That would test how far the screening signal generalizes.
segments.zh: 更广泛的贡献在于，它提供了一种方法，能把成功的智能体轨迹转化为对基础检查点的评估，前提是基准里有可执行的验证器。它跟智能体评估方面的研究形成互补，因为它问的是另一个问题：不只是看一个训练完成的智能体能不能成功，而是看一个训练程度较低的模型，在给定相关上下文时，能不能识别或生成一个经过验证的解题步骤。未来的研究应该用更大的样本群、更可控的后训练，以及跟每个目标任务族匹配的轨迹。这样才能检验这种筛选信号的泛化能力到底有多强。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So this is best treated as a screening tool, not a replacement for running the agent?
segments.zh: 所以这最好当作一种筛选工具，而不是替代跑智能体？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. The paper offers evidence that carefully chosen, verifier-grounded probes can help prioritize base checkpoints before costly post-training, while leaving full end-to-end evaluation essential. Its memorable idea is to move the evaluation point: instead of demanding that a base model solve everything from a cold start, test whether it can support the action that demonstrably makes a real task pass. That reveals useful potential, but does not erase the distinction between potential and independently sustained agent performance. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 没错。这篇论文提供的证据表明，经过精心挑选、以验证器为依据的探针，可以帮助在昂贵的后训练之前对基础检查点进行优先级排序，同时完整的端到端评估仍然必不可少。它令人印象深刻的想法是移动评估点：不再要求基础模型从冷启动解决一切，而是测试它是否能支持那个已被证明能让真实任务通过的动作。这揭示了有用的潜力，但并没有抹去潜力与独立维持的智能体表现之间的区别。感谢收听。如果你还有任何问题，可以询问我们的AI助手或留言评论。
